_strings.@@162af7753f7f: Colorado Child Tax Credit (2024 = regular credit + NEW Family Affordability Tax Credit) — Full-year and part-year Colorado residents (nonresidents are NOT eligible). The 2024 Colorado child tax credit computed on form DR 0104CN comprises BOTH: (a) the regular Colorado child tax credit — per qualifying child UNDER AGE 6 (born 2019 or later), not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $75,000 ($85,000 joint); and (b) the family affordability tax credit (NEW for 2024) — per qualifying child UNDER AGE 17 (born 2008 or later), not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $85,000 ($95,000 joint). Qualifying child follows the IRS Pub 501 relationship/residence/support/joint-return tests. Part-year residents apportion via DR 0104PN line 34.
_strings.@@1a1325164947: Treaty conformity — CO conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from CO income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the CO return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Colorado's DR 0104 begins at "Federal Taxable Income" (2024 line 1, "from your federal income tax form 1040, 1040 SR, or 1040 SP, line 15"). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income, so it flows through to Colorado untaxed UNLESS Colorado has an explicit addback. The 2024 DR 0104's complete Additions to Federal Taxable Income (lines 2-8) are: state income tax addback (Schedule A), Qualified Business Income Deduction addback, Standard/Itemized Federal Deduction addback (federal AGI over $300,000), business meals deduction addback (IRC 274(k) — NEW line 5 for 2024), nonqualified CollegeInvest distributions, nonqualified Colorado ABLE distributions, and Line 8 "Other Additions" (whose enumerated items in the 2024 booklet are: non-Colorado state/local bond interest, charitable conservation easement amounts also claimed for a CO credit, unauthorized alien labor expenses, partnership/fiduciary adjustments increasing federal taxable income, restricted-membership club expenses, and non-eligible medical savings account distributions). NONE of these is an addback of federally treaty-exempt or foreign-source income. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and Colorado conforms. (Confirmed against the official 2024 DR 0104 Book and the standalone 2024 DR 0104 form PDF on tax.colorado.gov.)

Tax line: DR 0104 Line 12 (Colorado Tax): full-year residents take the amount from the 2024 booklet tax table (built at 4.25%, printed through $50,000) for Line 11 Colorado Taxable Income (= Line 9 subtotal minus Line 10 subtractions); for Line 11 over $50,000 the booklet "Worksheet for taxable incomes over $50,000" multiplies Line 11 by 4.25% (.0425); part-year residents and nonresidents use the apportioned tax from the DR 0104PN. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change: the 2024 rate is 4.25% (down from 4.4% in 2023) — printed three ways in the 2024 DR 0104 Book (Line 12 instructions, the 2024 tax table header, and the over-$50,000 worksheet's X .0425). Colorado starts from federal TAXABLE income (DR 0104 Line 1) — the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, so Colorado has no exemptions or separate standard deduction. 2024 line renumbering: additions are Lines 2-8 (new Line 5 business-meals addback), subtotal Line 9, subtractions Line 10, Colorado Taxable Income Line 11, Colorado Tax Line 12 (2023: taxable income Line 10, tax Line 11). The DR 0104 form itself does not print a multiplication — Line 12 says to use the tax table (or the DR 0104PN apportionment). The booklet table is built at 4.25% but its $100-band midpoint rounding can differ from raw multiplication by a few dollars; the printed table row controls on the filed form.
